Anti-aliasing is the additional operations that use complex algorithms to remove or reduce the distortion caused by aliasing so that the end effect is better. It adds further computation to the overall computation of pixel intensities along with other rendering stages.
A dynamic scene is a scene that changes with user input.

A graphics library is a library that provides application programming interfaces (APIs) to deal with lower-level tasks, eliminating the need to know every detail of the underlying system or platform, such as processor, memory, or operating system detail, to build a graphics application.

Layered virtual reality software architecture is a VR software architecture arranged from top to bottom as an application layer, SDK layer, VR engine or game engine layer, native rendering library layer, operating system layer, and hardware layer, with each upper layer calling or sitting on the layer below.

A layered virtual reality system is a virtual reality system in which a software development kit (SDK) layer gives a developer access to a virtual reality engine that lets the developer deal with graphics through application programming interfaces (APIs) provided by native rendering libraries without directly accessing the native rendering libraries.
A multicore system is a system in which many cores, each capable only of simple integer and floating-point arithmetic, work simultaneously on a single instruction and produce data simultaneously.
A core is one of the many parts of a typically multicore GPU that is capable only of simple integer and floating-point arithmetic and works simultaneously on one instruction.

A streaming multiprocessor is a unit in a GPU made of several cores, each capable of simple integer and floating-point arithmetic, that work simultaneously on one single instruction, with a parallel data cache.
A thread execution manager is a part of a GPU that allocates work to many streaming multiprocessors.
Texture storage is high-speed storage on a graphics card that holds texture images, or predefined surface colors, which pixel calculations access to replace computed pixel colors with texture colors.

Projection stage is a GPU stage that combines viewing, projection, and viewport transformations in a composite matrix multiplied with vertices, producing a stream of triangles in screen or device coordinates ready to be converted to pixels.

A composite matrix is a matrix that combines viewing, projection, and viewport transformations in the GPU projection stage and is multiplied with vertices to produce triangles in screen or device coordinates.
Pixel processing stage is a GPU stage that performs surface texturing and hidden surface removal.

Surface texturing is an activity in the GPU pixel processing stage that, in its simplest method, applies stored texture images to the geometry being rendered by replacing the computed pixel color with the texture color at the corresponding texture point.

A depth buffer algorithm is an algorithm used in hidden surface removal that uses a dedicated depth buffer to store the depth information for points in a three-dimensional scene before projection onto a two-dimensional plane, where depth is the viewer's distance with respect to each pixel.

A depth buffer is a dedicated buffer used in hidden surface removal that stores the depth information for points in a three-dimensional scene before projection onto a two-dimensional plane, where depth is the viewer's distance with respect to each pixel.
An information point is a geographically spread place in a virtual tour that reveals related information for interactive exploration and contains many points of interest.
Oculus Quest 2 is a standalone computing device comprising a headset and handheld controllers, with its own processor and memory, that does not need to be tethered to a fixed computer.

The Majuli multimodal archive is a multimodal archive that consists of regular images, 360-degree images, and videos for indigenous architectural heritage of satras (Vaishnavite monasteries) and village life, 3D models for landscape and architecture, 2D drone shots for landscape, flora, and fauna, 2D videos for intangible cultural heritage, and textual descriptions.
A standalone computing device is a computing device comprising a headset and handheld controllers, with its own processor and memory, and that does not need to be tethered to a fixed computer.
An application is the top layer in a Unity layered architecture.

Cloud-based video loading optimization is an optimization that stores videos in the cloud and loads them when selected, rather than storing them locally, reducing storage and data-access requirements. It requires high bandwidth support, network coverage, and minimal latency to load high-quality videos in real time.

A cardboard virtual reality headset is a low-cost cardboard housing for a smartphone that, when the smartphone displays stereoscopic views and the housing is worn as a headset, provides an immersive environment without an expensive headset.
A Unity scene is a specific type of Unity asset that contains all or part of a game or application and is composed of game objects. Unity provides a scene interface to create, edit, or modify it.

Unity Hub is a standalone application whose installation is not mandatory. It is the primary way to install the Unity Editor and Unity Game Engine and streamlines finding, downloading, and managing Unity projects, installations, and multiple Unity versions.

Unity is a popular cross-platform game engine and developer environment that provides an editor interface and implementation support for the computer graphics pipeline, enabling developers to create, build, and deploy 2D and 3D interactive content, including XR experiences.

The computer graphics pipeline is a staged process that includes object definition, scene construction, color computation using lighting or shading models, view transformation, and scan conversion or rendering.

The unity editor interface is essentially an integrated development environment whose menu options provide developers the features required to build and deploy a system, and it allows developers to build and deploy realistic immersive environments without having to master and implement the computer graphics pipeline.
Unity Game Engine is middleware and an interface that allows developers to build extended reality experiences or systems and deploy them on a specific platform.

Scene view is the developer's interactive view that shows the scene being created in the Unity editor interface and lets the developer select, manipulate, and modify the game objects that together comprise the scene.

Game view is the final view in the Unity editor interface used to preview a developed scene, rendering the scene from the camera set by the developer to represent the final published or deployed application.

Game object is a fundamental object in Unity that represents characters, props, or a scenario and acts as a container for components that implement its functionality, so its properties are given by adding components.
A Unity asset is any item used in a Unity project to create an application. It can represent visual or audio elements and can be imported from outside Unity as a file or created inside Unity.
A Unity prefab is a template created by configuring and storing a Unity game object, allowing a user to make instances of that game object in a Unity scene.

A component is a Unity asset that can be added to a game object to implement part of the object's functionality or properties, and can be a built-in component type or a custom component created by scripting.
A primitive object type is an object type that can be created directly within Unity as a Unity game object.
A trigger is a Unity collider configured using the isTrigger property that does not behave as a solid object and allows other colliders to pass through.

A joint is a component of a physics engine that connects a rigid body to another rigid body or to a fixed point in space. It can apply forces that move the rigid bodies, has limits that restrict that movement, and is used to model realistic movement of objects or characters.

Material is a part of a model file that describes the appearance of an object's surface by specifying how it should be rendered, including references to textures, tiling information, color tints, and other information.
Texture is a stored bitmap image that is applied over a mesh surface to assign colors to pixels and that can represent other aspects of a material's surface, such as reflectivity and roughness.
Render pipeline support is a graphics support offered by Unity that supports implementation of the entire render pipeline and lets users have customized control over individual pipeline stages.
A render pipeline is a graphics pipeline that implements camera and view transform, lighting, meshes, materials, textures, shaders, and environment creation, and can be pre-built or custom.
Environment creation is a part of render pipeline support that creates world scenes or world-coordinate-system scenes, special environments such as skies, and different visual effects.
A pre-built render pipeline is a render pipeline provided by Unity, rather than a custom render pipeline created using Unity's scriptable render pipeline APIs.
Built-in render pipeline is one of Unity's pre-built render pipelines, with limited customization options.

The Universal Render Pipeline (URP) is a pre-built Unity render pipeline that provides a quick and easy way to customize graphics and create optimized graphics across a wide range of platforms, while the pipeline implementation takes care of pipeline-implementation optimization to some extent so resource requirements are minimized.

High Definition Render Pipeline (HDRP) is a pre-built, customizable Unity render pipeline that is intended to create high-fidelity, photorealistic graphics, but typically requires substantial resources and is meant for high-end platforms.
A custom render pipeline is a render pipeline that can be created by a developer using Unity's scriptable render pipeline APIs.

A model file is a file that represents a three-dimensional object by containing data on its shape and appearance, and may contain mesh, material, and texture data, as well as animation-related data if the object is an animated character.
A graphics primitive is, in Unity, mainly a three-dimensional mesh, with triangulated or quadrangulated polygonal meshes supported.
Mesh rendering workflow is a Unity workflow in which a mesh renderer takes geometry from a mesh filter and renders it at the position defined by a game object's transform component.
Mesh renderer is a renderer that takes geometry from the mesh filter and renders it at the position defined by the game object's transform component.
A bitmap image is an image applied over a mesh surface as a texture to assign basic color and many other aspects of a material's surface, such as reflectivity and roughness.
Scene creation is a process that involves transferring objects from local coordinates to world coordinates and using tools to create or modify environmental features.
The terrain tools preview package is a package that provides additional functionality on top of the built-in terrain features in the Unity editor.
The tree editor is a Unity editor tool that lets developers design trees directly in the editor.
A skybox is a sky background that a camera draws before rendering a frame, made as a cube with different textures on its faces to create the feel of a 360-degree environment and rendered at the back.
The halo effect is a visual effect that creates light areas around light sources, typically to give the impression of small dust particles in the air.
Lens flare effect is a visual effect that simulates the way lights refract inside a camera lens.

Line renderer effect is a visual effect that takes an array of two or more points in 3D space and draws a straight line between those points, allowing anything from a simple straight line to a complex spiral to be drawn.
A default graphics application programming interface is a Unity graphics application programming interface that accesses native graphics library application programming interfaces.

Autographics application programming interface is an option in Unity Player Settings that, when checked for a platform, makes a player build include a set of built-in graphics application programming interfaces and use the appropriate one at runtime; when unchecked, Unity's editor selects the first supported graphics application programming interface in the list of graphics application programming interfaces.

A built-in graphics application programming interface is one of a set of graphics application programming interfaces included in a Unity player build when the AutoGraphics application programming interface option is checked, with the appropriate one used at runtime to produce the best-case scenario for a platform.

The Unity physics engine is a physics engine that simulates physical laws in a project so that objects correctly accelerate and respond to collisions, using rigid bodies, colliders, joints, physics articulation, and character controllers to give a realistic feeling.
A rigid body is a physics component that, when attached to a game object, allows the object to respond to gravity, so falling or bouncing from a surface appears realistic.

A collider is a component in a physics engine that defines a game object's shape for physical collisions. It can be static, use primitive or mesh shapes, or be a trigger that other colliders pass through.

Physics articulation is a Unity component that represents the overall movement of a structure or object comprising joints, with its articulation body representing the joints as a constrained tree and automatically implementing joint constraints for realistic physics behavior.

The isKinematic property is a property used with a Unity rigid body that can remove an object from physics engine control, allowing a script to move it kinematically and letting the developer choose whether it follows gravity.
A primitive collider is a type of collider in Unity, such as a box, sphere, or capsule collider, that defines the shape of a game object for physical collisions.
A physics material is a Unity material that is used to configure the friction and bounce of a surface.

An articulation body is a class or component that represents an articulation as a logical tree of joints, whose parent-child relationships reflect mutually constrained relative motion, and automatically implements joint constraints so a complex figure can move realistically without controlling each joint.

A logical tree is a representation of an articulation body in which each node is a joint and each parent-child relationship reflects mutually constrained relative motion, so the relations and relative movements of the joints define the overall articulation.

An animation system is a system that supports importing, aligning, and previewing animation clips, retargeting humanoid animations, transitions and interactions between animations, and animating different body parts with different logics.
Humanoid animation retargeting is the ability to apply animations from one character model onto another.
Audio source is the primary Unity component attached to a game object to make it play a sound, allowing an audio clip to be played back when triggered through a mixer, code, or by default.

Audio listener is a Unity component that listens to all audio playing in the scene and transfers it to computer speakers; all heard audio is with respect to its positioning, and by default only one should be in the scene, attached to the camera.
An audio filter is a Unity component that modifies the output of an audio source or the intake of an audio listener to generate various sound effects.
Audio clip is a standard audio file that can be played back by a Unity audio source when triggered.
Position is the component of pose that specifies the location of a three-dimensional point, represented by three coordinates in a vector.

A unity script is a C# script that can be attached as a component to a game object to control its behavior, letting it trigger events, modify component properties over time, and respond to user input when the game runs.
C-sharp is an object-oriented programming language that Unity supports as its scripting language.
A start function is an initialization event function in a Unity script that is called as the starting point whenever the script is called.
An update function is a Unity script function that is called in each frame.
Vector3 is a data type that represents the position of a three-dimensional point by storing three coordinates as three elements of a vector.
A three-dimensional point is a position represented by three coordinates stored as the three elements of a vector.
The debug.log function is a function in a Unity script that prints a message to console output, which can be seen after running the game or application or after the script has been executed.
Destroy function is a function in Unity's MonoBehaviour class that destroys a game object from the scene after a specified delay, typically in seconds.
A user-defined function is a function that is defined by the user, rather than prebuilt, and is typically part of a good script.
An event function is a Unity function that Unity activates in response to an event during gameplay, passing control to it so its body executes and then returning control to Unity.
Physics event is a Unity gameplay event function that relates to contact being made or broken.
A physics-related event is a Unity gameplay event function that is called when a collider is configured as a trigger.
The OnTriggerEnter function is a Unity physics-related event function that is called when a collider is configured as a trigger.
The OnTriggerExit function is a Unity physics-related event function that is called when a collider is configured as a trigger.

A loop is a scripting-environment construct that executes a loop body under a loop condition, with entry-controlled loops checking the condition before the body and exit-controlled loops checking the condition after at least one execution.
An entry-controlled loop is a type of loop in a scripting environment in which the loop condition is checked before the loop body executes.
An exit-controlled loop is a loop in a scripting environment whose body executes at least once and whose condition is checked after the loop body executes.
A for loop is an entry-controlled loop in a scripting environment that checks the loop condition before the loop body executes.
A while loop is an entry-controlled loop in a scripting environment whose loop condition is checked before the loop body executes.
A loop condition is the condition in a loop that is checked either before the loop body executes, in entry-controlled loops, or after the loop body executes, in exit-controlled loops.
A do-while loop is an exit-controlled loop in a scripting environment, in which the loop body executes at least once and the loop condition is checked after the loop body executes.

A for each loop is a loop that can be used for arrays or collections of homogeneous data types, allowing the programmer to work with the collection directly instead of dealing with individual data types.
The transform property is a property attached to every game object in a scene that stores the object's position, rotation, and scale and can be modified programmatically through a script.

A coroutine is a method that allows a developer to spread tasks across several frames by pausing execution, returning control, and continuing where it left off on the following frame; it does not create threads and its operations still execute on the main thread.
Opacity fade is a gradual reduction of an object's alpha or opacity over a sequence of frames so that intermediate values are rendered and visible.
InvokeRepeating is a method that takes a function name and two times in seconds, invoking the function after the initial delay and then repeatedly at the repeat interval.
Initial delay is a time value, in seconds, that specifies how long to wait before a repeatedly invoked method first starts.
An interval is a specified time in seconds that sets how often a method is repeatedly invoked after an initial delay.
Build is the process in the Unity development environment that creates a package for a selected platform from the selected scenes, so the system can be published or deployed.

The Build Settings window is a Unity editor window that contains the settings and options for publishing a built system, including the scenes in the build, the selected platform, and the Build or Build and Run button that begins the build process.
File Build Settings is the Unity editor path used to reach the Build Settings window, which contains all settings and options to publish or deploy a build.
Scenes in Build panel is a panel in the Build Settings window of the Unity development environment's editor that manages which scenes are included in a build.
The Build button is a button in the Unity editor's Build Settings window that begins the build process.
The Build and Run button is a button in the Unity development environment's editor that begins the build process.

Unity layered architecture is a layered architecture in which the application is the top layer and a software development kit (SDK) layer above the Unity layer is treated as part of the installed Unity package.

A software development kit layer is a layer in a Unity layered architecture, positioned on top of the Unity layer, that is treated as part of the installed Unity package whose application programming interfaces are used.

Vuforia setup is the process in which a new database is created on the Vuforia website, images or markers to be tracked are added to that database, and the downloaded database package file is imported into the project so the Vuforia engine can recognize them.
An image target behavior script is a script that is attached to or used to modify the behavior of a Vuforia image target and performs the operations after the Vuforia engine recognizes the marker.
An android package (APK) is a file created when building for the Android platform that can be deployed directly to an Android device or transferred and installed separately.
